context: A home worth this or less on 1 April 1991 is in Band A, the lowest band.

label: Band B: highest value in England (1 April 1991)
context: Band B covers values above Band A's limit, up to this.

label: Band C: highest value in England (1 April 1991)
context: Band C covers values above Band B's limit, up to this.

label: Band D: highest value in England (1 April 1991)
context: Band D covers values above Band C's limit, up to this. Councils quote their Council Tax as a Band D amount.

label: Band E: highest value in England (1 April 1991)
context: Band E covers values above Band D's limit, up to this.

label: Band F: highest value in England (1 April 1991)
context: Band F covers values above Band E's limit, up to this.

label: Band G: highest value in England (1 April 1991)
context: Band G covers values above Band F's limit, up to this. Anything above is Band H, the highest band in England.

label: Band A: highest value in Wales (1 April 2003)

label: Band C: highest value in Wales (1 April 2003)
context: Band C covers values above Band B's limit, up to this.

label: Band D: highest value in Wales (1 April 2003)

subcategory_description: Council Tax bands and the rules on tenancy deposits.
subject_intro: How much deposit a landlord can take in England, how soon they must protect it, and what happens if they don't.
subject_meta_title: Tenancy Deposits in England: Cap of 5 Weeks' Rent and 30-Day Rule
subject_meta_description: Tenancy deposits in England are capped at 5 weeks' rent (6 weeks if the annual rent is £50,000 or more) and must be protected within 30 days.
label: Most a deposit can be (annual rent under £50,000)
context: A landlord or agent cannot take more than this as a tenancy deposit in England. Anything above it is a prohibited payment.

label: Most a deposit can be (annual rent £50,000 or more)
context: The higher cap that applies to expensive tenancies in England.

label: Annual rent at which the higher cap applies
context: A tenancy with an annual rent of this or more can have a deposit of up to 6 weeks' rent.

label: Most a holding deposit can be
context: A holding deposit reserves a property before the tenancy starts. It's separate from the tenancy deposit.

label: Time a landlord has to protect the deposit
context: From the day they get it, the landlord must tell the tenant how it's protected in an approved scheme.

label: Most a court can order a landlord to repay on top of the deposit
context: A court can order this if the deposit wasn't protected when it should have been, and tenants can apply at any time during the tenancy.
